what: Which large lower facades a player actually sees, and whether there is licence-clean evidence to give any of them building-specific ground-floor articulation.
verdict: NO IMPLEMENTATION. The highest-value facade was identified and the generator limitation was pinned down, but no licence-clean building-specific ground-floor or ordinary-entrance evidence is reachable, and the uniformity that reads generic turns out to be a DOCUMENTED, DELIBERATE Wave-A finding rather than an oversight.

Ell/Curry.verdict: CORRECTLY PLACED. It is on the quad-facing frontage and inside the frustum from both quad viewpoints - 33.5 m at V3, 19.3 m at V5. Retain; do not add a second door beside it.

Dodge Hall.verdict: FACES AWAY. Dodge presents 54.4 per cent of the canonical frame width to the quad with NO entrance cue on that face, while its single cue sits on the south-east side, away from every tested gameplay viewpoint. This is a real finding and it is actionable - but the cue position is FACTUAL, derived from a PDDL walk termination, so it must not be moved. What is missing is evidence for a quad-facing door, not a reason to relocate the evidenced one.

phase5_generatorLimitation.mechanism: TYPO.neuHistoric sets strip: true, so Facades.pierStorey lays full-storey brick piers with a recessed channel between them for EVERY storey including the ground one, and sets stoneGround: false, so there is no contrasting base storey. A pedestrian at 17 m sees one unbroken vertical-strip wall from the 0.70 m plinth to the cornice, with a single 2.6 m entrance cue on a very long frontage.
phase5_generatorLimitation.butItIsDeliberate: TYPO.neuHistoric documents this in its own comment: "No stone ground storey: this family is one masonry from plinth to cornice, over a modest granite base, and a contrasting stone storey is the Boston collegiate move it was specifically NOT built with." Wave A reasoned it from the documented architecture and raised the plinth from 0.40 to 0.70 m - the largest of the four typologies - to carry the base on its own.
phase5_generatorLimitation.consequence: Restoring a stone ground storey would contradict a documented Wave-A finding and would make the range LESS like Northeastern. Rejected.

screenSpaceImportance.why: To answer the Wave-D question 'does a player actually see this frontage' with occlusion rather than bearing.
screenSpaceImportance.method: Live engine, runtime camera (fov 62, 1920x1080). 45 samples per plane (9 across x 5 up). Frustum test, then a ray from the eye to each sample against all 303 visible scene meshes with a 0.75 m epsilon. Samples with camera-space z < 2 are rejected so near-plane leakage cannot fabricate a bbox — the failure mode that produced a screen-x of -720909 in D0.

whyTheGateFailed.theShortVersion: D2B was legitimate because POSITION came from data and only SIZE was authored. For Dodge's quad frontage there is no positional datum at all, so implementing would mean authoring the position too — that is inventing a door, which the brief forbids.
d2bHadThreeAnchorsDodgeHasNone: 1. An official sentence stating entry from the quad — Ell: 'When you enter Ell Hall from Krentzman Quad'. Dodge: NO equivalent sentence exists in any of the five sources.
2. A factual PDDL walk cue ON that frontage — Ell: part 661061 edge 80, a real sidewalk dead-end against the facade. Dodge: the only cue is edge 20 on the north face, facing away (-0.52).
3. Therefore D2B only RESIZED an existing factual opening and never chose where it went. For Dodge there is nothing to resize; a new opening would have to be placed.
whyTheGateFailed.theWalkDataWasCheckedAndIsEmpty: NEU_WALK_REJECTED is [] — nothing was discarded that could help. The nearest shipped walk, id 13932, dead-ends at (-1855.08, 1689.15), which is 19.48 m off the edge-12 plane. It terminates in open quad, not against Dodge. So the 'refetch the walk set' route recorded in FRONT_QUAD.json is genuinely still open, but it has not been done and nothing currently in the repo substitutes for it.
whyTheGateFailed.whyEdge12WouldHaveBeenTaste: Edge 12 is the tempting answer: central of three planes, most head-on at facing 0.998, and the closest. But 'most head-on plane' is a GEOMETRIC property, not evidence of a door. Placing an opening on edge 12 rather than edge 10 or edge 15 would be three unfalsifiable choices across 61.5 m of frontage, and there is no source that discriminates between them. In D2B it was possible to write 'the edge chose the number, not taste' because a factual cue fixed the position and the edge length bounded the width. Here nothing fixes the position, so the honest sentence would have been 'I chose it', which is the sentence the brief exists to prevent.
whyTheGateFailed.theBriefsOwnTest: 'If exact coordinates cannot be supported but a broad central facade zone is VISUALLY UNAMBIGUOUS ...' — nothing was visually observed. Every reachable source is TEXT. The one class of evidence that could have made the zone visually unambiguous, official photography, returns HTTP 418, re-confirmed this wave. The condition is not met, so the fallback clause applies: FAIL cleanly. Do not create a door.
whyTheGateFailed.aggravatingFact: Dodge is a 1954 library converted to a business school and renovated in 1993. Even a confident architectural intuition about a 1950s library frontage would not transfer to the current building with any reliability.

phase4_acceptedStandard.source: tools/neu-walks/build.mjs, entranceCues() — read directly rather than inferred
rules: TYPE must be PWALK-CL. Line 1 of the loop is `if (f.attributes.TYPE !== 'PWALK-CL') continue;` — SWALK-CL public sidewalk is explicitly NOT entrance evidence.
Only path ENDPOINTS are tested, indices [0, length-1]. Mid-segment proximity never qualifies.
ENTRANCE_MAX_FACE_M = 2.0 — the endpoint must be within 2.0 m of the part ring. Its comment: 'a genuine dead-end at the wall, not a passer-by'.
The matched ring edge must be at least 5 m long (n.edgeLen < 5 is skipped).
One cue per part: the termination with the SMALLEST face distance wins.
t is clamped to [0.18, 0.82] and x/z is recomputed from the clamped t, to keep cues off quoins.
fromWay IS the ArcGIS OBJECTID — `fromWay: f.attributes.OBJECTID`.
phase4_acceptedStandard.importantConsequence: Because only the CLOSEST termination per part survives, the shipped artefact could never have answered this wave's question. It records that Dodge's winner is edge 20 at 0.91 m; it is silent on whether other terminations exist elsewhere on the building. D2D enumerated ALL of them instead of trusting the winner.
phase4_acceptedStandard.standardNotLoosened: The same thresholds were applied to Dodge unchanged. No new, looser rule was invented to let Dodge pass.

everyQualifyingTerminationAgainstDodgeAn.note: This is the EXISTING southeast cue, reproduced bit-for-bit from the live service: edge 20, faceDistM 0.91, edgeLenM 22.52, fromWay 56330. The pipeline is confirmed sound.

nearMissesAndWhyTheyFail.closestApproach: start endpoint 1.29 m from ring edge 11 — the closest ANY endpoint gets to the quad frontage
nearMissesAndWhyTheyFail.failsBecause: Three independent reasons. (1) TYPE is SWALK-CL, which the accepted standard excludes from entrance evidence. (2) The matched edge 11 is 1.15 m long, below the 5 m minimum — it is a corner connector, not a facade. (3) Its heading against the facade normal is -0.01, i.e. it runs PARALLEL to the frontage. It is a sidewalk going PAST Dodge, which is precisely the 'passer-by' the 2.0 m rule exists to reject.

nearMissesAndWhyTheyFail.closestApproach: start endpoint 6.78 m from ring edge 10, heading +1.00 against that plane's normal

nearMissesAndWhyTheyFail.failsBecause: 6.78 m is 3.4x the accepted 2.0 m threshold — stretching to reach it is exactly what the brief forbade. And the decisive fact: it is NOT a dead end. Two public sidewalks, OBJECTID 72312 (start) and 95997 (end), share that endpoint at 0.00 m. It is a path JUNCTION in open quad, and 97731 runs AWAY from it to the northwest. That is real circulation evidence and it corroborates that the quad frontage is walked. It is NOT a door anchor, and no reading of it produces one.

phase5_decision.notOutcomeC: Relevant centrelines DO exist near the frontage, so this is not an empty result.

This is not an argument for placing one on edge 10 either — a junction 6.78 m out in open quad, shared by two sidewalks and running away, is not evidence of a door.

pddlMatch.neighbourContamination: NONE. 335A Huntington's centroid is 25.06 m away, outside the 24 m match radius; both parts sit 8.6/8.7 m from 337's centroid against 26.1/27.4 m from 335A's. A swept-in 335A would require ~1,224 m2, not 813.

storeyReconciliation.derivedPipelineAlreadyGave5: YES — round(18.46 / 3.8) = 5, so the value was retained and only its provenance changed, from DERIVED to owner-published confidence B.
storeyReconciliation.grossAreaImplicationSuperseded: The inventory's ~5.9 was never a storey count. It is an INDIRECT implication from 50,023 sq ft of gross area over a 783 m2 footprint. Owner-published Northeastern evidence states 5 stories directly, and direct evidence supersedes the implication, so the two are not in conflict. WHY the gross-area arithmetic evaluates to about 5.9 is NOT established by any currently accepted evidence: basement area, footprint-definition differences and gross-area accounting conventions would each account for the gap, none of them is evidenced here, and none is promoted to fact. CORRECTION: an earlier version of this entry asserted the basement explanation outright. That went beyond the evidence and is withdrawn.

typology.why: 337 is in neither NEU_HISTORIC nor TYPO_OF, so typoFor falls through to the default.
typology.explicitly: This is the existing generic pre-1960 FALLBACK. It is NOT a claim that 337 has Richards-family architecture, and no bespoke 337 family was invented.
typology.knownLimitation: `collegiate` carries stoneGround: true, so the model shows a stone ground storey. For a 1923 brick apartment block that is a generic institutional treatment rather than evidenced fact. Recorded rather than silently accepted or silently 'fixed', because inventing a residential typology is exactly what the brief forbade.

waveD3Result.entranceDecision: NONE BUILT. The stair entry is factual in existence and unlocated. Same rule that closed Dodge in D2C/D2D: existence is not position. No entrance, no steps, no landing, no canopy, no ramp, no signage.

proceduralReplacement.mechanism: At source. Districts.inHeroFootprint blocks plot generation and Buildings.heroOverlap filters plots; both read NEU_HERO_PARTS, so adding 337 suppresses automatically. No mesh was hidden.
proceduralReplacement.verdict: Exactly one procedural building removed per 337 part. No duplicate building, no duplicate collider.

campusGroundSideEffect.theFlaw: GROUND.near is a radius and a radius knows nothing about roads. 337's two masses sit 74.5 and 87.9 m from the quad centre, inside the 110 m radius, so the dilated hull reached ACROSS Huntington.

measuredHarmIfUnfixed.reading: Essentially ALL new ground would have landed across the arterial, around a residential parcel — the prohibited outcome. The road keep-out held (rejections 2,920 -> 6,532 m2) so nothing reached the carriageway, but it says nothing about ground beyond it.

campusGroundSideEffect.fix: One predicate in NeuHero._buildGround's contour selection: a part reachable from the quad centre only by CROSSING the Huntington centreline does not define the opening's ground. Continuity, not distance. Implemented as a proper segment-intersection test, not a side-of-nearest-segment sign, which is unreliable near a curving centreline.
campusGroundSideEffect.predicateVerified: All 9 already-selected parts return false; both 337 parts return true.
campusGroundSideEffect.scope: Contour selection only. footEdges/reach was left untouched; both candidate fixes measured identically, so the smaller was taken.

resultMeasuredLive.note: All four match the figures C-2B recorded independently. The ground did not move.

campusGroundSideEffect.rejected: z-offsets, epsilon widening, or hiding the surface.

The admissible measurement is therefore signal inside 337's projected silhouette against control outside it, in the SAME frame pair.

visibility.refinementToD0: D0 said 'visible from two gameplay viewpoints'. Measured: visible from three (V2, V3, V5) and NOT from the canonical opening V1, where the player faces into the quad and 337 is behind. It becomes visible the moment the player looks toward Huntington, which is V3 and V5.

waveD3Result.nextScope: The Huntington frontage is now closed at its most-seen gap. The remaining D0 coverage candidates were all measured as fully occluded from every gameplay viewpoint, so coverage is no longer the dominant defect there. The most valuable next target is eye-level fidelity on what the player DOES see from the opening: the collegiate stoneGround treatment now visible on 337 is the clearest evidence-thin detail this wave exposed, and 335A Huntington (441 m2, leased, adjacent) is the only remaining unmodelled parcel on the same frontage.

waveD4Result.what: Krentzman Huntington gateway — the brick Northeastern sign / seal ledge
waveD4Result.verdict: BLOCKED. Docs only, no runtime change. TWO independent gates fail: position and screen value.
waveD4Result.headline: The object is one of the best-evidenced things in this whole programme — three official sources, unambiguous. What cannot be defended is WHERE it goes, and separately, whether a player would ever see the thing that makes it worth having.

officialEvidenceVerified.quote: Flanked by Dodge, Richards, and Ell halls, Krentzman Quad is one of the campus' primary gateways. The brick ledge at the entrance to the quad—emblazoned with the university's seal—is a popular spot for new graduates to pose for photos in celebration of their academic achievements.
officialEvidenceVerified.establishes: existence; brick; at the quad entrance; the university seal; the flanking halls; the photo tradition

officialEvidenceVerified.quote: Beware, the line is often long, but photos sitting on the Northeastern sign in front of Krentzman along Huntington Avenue are a must for any grad.
officialEvidenceVerified.establishes: along Huntington Avenue, in front of Krentzman — and, unusually useful, that people SIT ON IT, which is a real constraint on height

officialEvidenceVerified.quote: the iconic brick Northeastern sign located along Huntington Avenue
officialEvidenceVerified.establishes: brick and Huntington-side, independently of source 2

waveD4Result.alreadyKnownHere: Not a new discovery: docs/neu/SOURCES.md already cited the 2016 article, SPAWN_CANDIDATES.json already called the ledge 'the graduation photo spot', and CURRENT_VS_REAL.md's scoring row already listed its absence as a defect. D4 is the first wave to test whether it can actually be built.
waveD4Result.correctionToEarlierProjectWording: An earlier scoring row describes it as 'no seal ledge at the quad head'. The three sources place it at the ENTRANCE, along Huntington — the mouth of the quad, not its head. Recorded here rather than by rewriting a dated audit row.

confidenceTable.B. belongs to the Krentzman Quad entranc: HIGH — 'at the entrance to the quad', 'in front of Krentzman'
confidenceTable.I. exact height: LOW — not stated. Bounded only by the fact that graduates sit on it, which implies roughly seat height. That is an inference about scale, not a dimension.
confidenceTable.J. brick colour / material: MEDIUM for 'brick', stated twice. UNKNOWN for colour, bond or coping.
confidenceTable.L. lettering / wordmark treatment: UNKNOWN — no source describes any lettering at all

gate1_position.theZone: The quad's open sector runs 110 degrees between ring vertices 8 (-1901.9, 1692.1) and 9 (-1846.0, 1666.5) — a mouth chord of 61.5 m. 'At the entrance, along Huntington' constrains DEPTH well and lateral position not at all.
gate1_position.depthIsDefensible: The usable band is campus ground about 20 m off the Huntington centreline: 5.24 m clear of the 14.76 m road keep-out, flat at surfaceHeight 3.095-3.097, district northeastern, and 3.5-4.0 m from the factual PDDL arrival walk. That much IS pinned by accepted geometry.
gate1_position.lateralIsNot: Along the 61.5 m mouth there is no factual datum whatsoever. Every position from t=0.2 to t=0.8 satisfies all three official statements equally.
gate1_position.noSurveyFeatureCapturesIt: Checked. The cached PDDL Roof Breaks layer holds exactly one part under 250 m2 within 70 m of the quad centre, and it is a 26.74 m building mass, not a ledge. Roof Breaks is a BUILDINGS layer; a half-metre garden wall is not a building and will never appear in it.

photographsCannotConstrainIt.drsFilePages: HTTP 418 to automated fetch, as recorded twice before
photographsCannotConstrainIt.nuhistoryItemPage: reachable (200) — neu:183404, 'Northeastern University sign in front of Krentzman Quad and Ell Hall', [ca. 1903-2009], photographer Joshua D. Levine
photographsCannotConstrainIt.butTheMetadataIsSilent: The title is the whole description. It gives no side, no orientation, and no relationship to Huntington. A title naming Ell in the background does not discriminate between positions along a 61.5 m mouth.
photographsCannotConstrainIt.andTheRightsAreNotCleared: Rights statement verbatim: 'Copyright Not Evaluated. The copyright and related rights status of this Item has not been evaluated.' By this project's own standing discipline, absence of a stated restriction is not a grant.

gate1_position.northeasternArcgis: Not consulted for coordinates. It is audit-reference-only under the project's source policy, and hand-copying its coordinates would be the same act with worse provenance.
gate1_position.whyThisIsNotJustCaution: This is the D2C standard applied unchanged. Dodge's quad frontage was also 61.5 m, and the wave refused to pick a plane because 'most head-on' is geometry, not evidence. Here the fallback would be centring the ledge on the quad axis — which is exactly the aesthetic symmetry the brief names as insufficient. Placing it by symmetry and labelling it project-authored would not make the choice any more falsifiable.
gate1_position.oneAwkwardConsequence: The most 'natural' looking positions are also where the player spawns: the t=0.35 candidate lands 2.3 m from the canonical spawn. Any authored placement would have to dodge the spawn, which is a further authored decision on top of an already authored one.

gate2_screenValue.method: Envelope probe, no geometry added: a 10 m x 0.50 m ledge at each of five candidate positions, sampled 11 x 3 and ray-tested against every visible scene mesh from the live world. Analytic projection cross-checked it. Raycasts are CPU-side, so the hidden-pane compositing problem noted below does not touch these numbers.

results.V1 canonical opening: NOT IN FRUSTUM at any candidate. The player spawns facing INTO the quad (yaw -2.007, 25 degrees off the quad centre), so the whole Huntington-side band sits 54 to 130 degrees off axis against a 46.9 degree half-HFOV. The eastern candidates miss the frustum edge by about 7 degrees.
results.V3 Krentzman centre -> Huntington: 308-337 px wide by 14 px TALL, 0.21-0.23 per cent of screen. Unoccluded fraction 0.00 / 0.18 / 0.73 / 0.97 / 0.82 across the five positions — the western end is entirely hidden.
results.V4 Huntington sidewalk -> campus: 293-353 x 15 px, 0.21-0.26 per cent, unoccluded 0.55-0.67, and the UNOCCLUDED box is only 7 px tall: half the ledge is behind something at every position.
results.V2 Huntington turn: fully unoccluded but 61 x 14 px (0.04 per cent) at the far end, reaching 672 x 114 px (3.69 per cent) only at the candidate 13 m from the eye.

gate2_screenValue.occluders: prop:veg_shrub2 (23 of 25 blocked samples) and an American elm. Existing planting in the band is roughly the height of the whole object.
gate2_screenValue.versusTheBriefsBenchmarks: 337 Huntington measures 6.1 per cent of screen at V3. This ledge measures 0.21-0.23 per cent at the same viewpoint — about 27x smaller, and 14 px tall.
gate2_screenValue.theIdentityIsTheProblem: The wall itself would read as a thin horizontal line. The thing that makes it worth building — the seal and any lettering — does not resolve: a 0.50 m face is 20 px at 25 m and 33 px at 15 m, so cap height lands at 8 and 13 px. A 0.35 m seal is 14 px at 25 m. It becomes legible at about 8 m, standing next to it.
gate2_screenValue.theBriefsOwnTest: 'If it is effectively sub-pixel / fully hidden: do not implement merely because it is iconic in reality.' It is not literally sub-pixel, but its identity content is unresolvable at every gameplay viewpoint, and it is absent from the canonical opening entirely. That is the same failure mode as the station-name blade the brief cites as the negative benchmark, and the honest answer to 'does it outperform tiny station lettering' is no.

gate3_brandingRecordedNotExercised.status: Not reached — position and screen value fail first. Recorded so a future wave does not re-derive it.
gate3_brandingRecordedNotExercised.existingPrecedent: Landmarks._makeCitgo draws the Citgo sign from GENERIC canvas primitives — two triangles and Helvetica text — with no imported artwork. That is the project's de facto policy for real-world marks, and it is a good one: procedural approximation from ordinary primitives, never a downloaded asset.
gate3_brandingRecordedNotExercised.noWrittenPolicy: There is no trademark or logo section in AGENTS.md, CONTRACTS.md or SOURCES.md. The Citgo code is the only precedent, so it is worth writing down.
gate3_brandingRecordedNotExercised.theSealSpecifically: Factual existence of the seal is HIGH. That is entirely separate from a right to reproduce the seal artwork. The only reachable image of the object carries 'Copyright Not Evaluated', which is not a grant, and tracing artwork out of a photograph would be worse provenance than using it directly.
gate3_brandingRecordedNotExercised.ifEverBuilt: Brick architecture first; a plain textual treatment only if ordinary nominative naming is acceptable; a clearly project-authored non-logo medallion at most. Never a downloaded seal, never a traced wordmark.

whatWasNotDone: No ledge, wall, sign, medallion or lettering was created.
No geometry was added anywhere. src/ is byte-identical to HEAD.
No Krentzman ring, campus ground, Huntington, Green Line, spawn, SUV, 337, Ell or Dodge change.
No seal or wordmark artwork was downloaded, traced or approximated.
Northeastern ArcGIS was not consulted for coordinates.
whatWouldUnblockIt: A licence-clean survey or City feature that captures the ledge itself — it is not in Roof Breaks and is unlikely to be in any buildings layer, so this probably means a structures or street-furniture dataset if one exists under acceptable terms.
An official Northeastern source that states which side of the quad mouth it stands on, or a rights-cleared image whose metadata does.

NOTE that even with position solved, gate 2 still fails at 0.21-0.23 per cent of screen with unresolvable identity. Position alone does not make this worth building; it would also need a reason a player ever sees it, which at the canonical opening they do not.
waveD4Result.instrumentNote: One screenshot came back part-composited and a second attempt timed out on requestAnimationFrame: document.hidden was true, and rAF does not fire in a hidden pane. Only the visual channel was affected. Every number above comes from CPU-side raycasting and analytic projection. The engine was verified still running afterwards, with 0 errors, 0 glFaults and validate ok.
